verdict.rationale: Increase documents that it separates Accounts from Account Numbers in a one-to-many mapping. Developers can instantly create multiple Account Numbers per Account programmatically and give each customer or counterparty a unique number, so incoming funds reconcile automatically across ACH, wire, RTP and check. Customer stories describe per-user accounts (Ramp) and FBO account structures (Ascend). Missing for 10: an explicitly documented hierarchical sub-account/master-account model, stated scale limits or throughput figures for number issuance, and independent hands-on corroboration beyond vendor docs and customer stories.

support.subject: As a developer, I can issue unique account and routing numbers at scale — virtual accounts for reconciliation, per-customer collection accounts, and sub-accounts under a master structure

citations.quote: You can instantly create multiple Account Numbers for a single Account and manage them programmatically.

With Increase, you can issue each investor a unique Account Number. This allows for automatic reconciliation of any received funds from that investor, regardless of how they send funds (via Wire, RTP, ACH, or even Check).
This allows for a one-to-many mapping, providing much greater flexibility for new use cases.
Ramp spins up unique accounts per user, allowing the team to programmatically track payments instead of needing to parse through a single, massive ledger.
Reconcile inbound payments by providing each counterparty with a unique Account Number to automatically match them with any incoming credits or debits.
